summary: Move attention between views while preserving user control and object state.
objective: Move attention between views while preserving user control and object state.
example_prompts: Use interruptible focus transition for the scene, preserving its model and user controls.

principles: Camera easing is a presentation choice; it must not drive the underlying model.
A new navigation input should have a clear policy for replacing or interrupting an existing transition.
implementation: Capture the current camera and target as the transition start, including when interrupted.
Frame the selected bounds with suitable near-plane clearance; retain a reset view.
Allow a reduced-motion or immediate-focus path when requested by the user or host preference.
observable_checks: Rapid focus changes finish at the last requested object without a delayed snap to an older target.
Pausing world motion still permits inspection unless the interface explicitly says otherwise.

creative_affordances: Adapt the layout, visual treatment and timing to the task; these are reusable design proposals, not mandatory templates.
known_limits: Authored interaction/presentation guidance; no new scientific claim, accessibility certification or runtime verification is asserted.
